subject: SIG: Clarify ambiguous data-flow / S3 access (Bluebridge)
messages:
From: Jordan Price <jordan.price@bluebridgebank.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: SIG — Q12b (S3 access) needs clarification

Hi Mina,

Thanks for sending over the SIG draft earlier. Our security team reviewed the answers and flagged Q12b (data ingress/egress and object-level S3 access) as ambiguous for our procurement checklist. Two specific asks from our side: 

1) Please confirm whether Redwood requires any cross-account IAM roles that would grant write permissions to customer-owned S3 buckets, or whether ingestion always uses a customer-managed ingestion path (presigned URLs or a customer push).
2) If you rely on a cross-account role for read access (for model caching/replication), can you explicitly state the minimal permissions and whether KMS CMKs in the customer account are required?

We prefer a short written statement that we can attach to the SIG answers. If it's easier, a quick 20-minute call with our security engineer (security-team@bluebridgebank.com) would also work.

Can you confirm? We have a procurement deadline next week (target sign-off 2027-04-12).

Thanks,
Jordan

Senior Security Engineer, Bluebridge Bank

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@bluebridgebank.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG — Q12b (S3 access) needs clarification

Hi Jordan — thanks for the clear ask and the deadline head's up.

Short answer up front: Redwood does NOT require write access to customer S3 buckets. We support two common ingestion patterns and will include explicit wording in the SIG:

- Customer-push (recommended): Customer uploads objects to their own S3 bucket. Redwood reads from the customer bucket using a customer-created cross-account read-only IAM role (sts:AssumeRole) with granular permissions (s3:GetObject, s3:ListBucket) and, if objects are encrypted, kms:Decrypt on the customer CMK. Redwood never writes to customer buckets in this flow.

- Customer-provided presigned-URLs: For simple blob uploads we support presigned PUT URLs generated in the customer environment; Redwood receives objects via our ingestion endpoints. In this flow no cross-account role is required. Note: we do not rely on presigned URLs for server-to-server ingestion that requires guaranteed non-repudiation — those customers typically use the cross-account read role.

Attached: draft SIG answers (SIG-Bluebridge-Draft-Answers-20270403.pdf) and a simple network/data-flow diagram (network-diagram-bluebridge.png).

I'll propose a concise written statement for the SIG below — please review and let us know if it addresses both of your points. If you want a short call, I'm available Mon/Tue mornings PST.

Proposed SIG wording (draft):
"Redwood Inference does not require write permissions into customer-owned S3 buckets. For data ingestion, customers may either (a) push objects via presigned URLs generated in the customer environment, or (b) grant a customer-managed cross-account IAM role with read-only permissions (s3:GetObject, s3:ListBucket). When customer-owned KMS CMKs are used to encrypt objects, Redwood requires kms:Decrypt permission for the provided CMK. Redwood only assumes the cross-account role to read objects and does not modify or delete customer data in the bucket."

If that looks good, we'll finalize the SIG response and add the minimal permission block we use for our implementation.

Regards,
Mina Haddad
Enterprise Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG — Q12b (S3 access) needs clarification

Mina — good draft. Two suggested edits before we send final to Jordan/security: 

1) Add explicit line stating we do not use presigned URLs for automated server-to-server ingestion that requires non-repudiation. Jordan called this out; better to be explicit: "Redwood does not rely on presigned URLs for server-to-server bulk ingestion in production; customers who require guaranteed provenance should use the cross-account role."

2) KMS nuance: clarify that customer CMKs are optional — if customer bucket objects are encrypted with a customer-owned CMK, Redwood requires kms:Decrypt; if objects are encrypted with a Redwood-managed key or not encrypted, the customer CMK is not required. This avoids implying we always need customers to create CMKs.

Suggested final paragraph to include minimal permissions (paste into SIG):
"Example minimal IAM trust and permissions for cross-account read-only access:
- Trust: customer-account:role/RedwoodCrossAccountReadRole (sts:AssumeRole)
- Permissions (attached policy): s3:ListBucket (on arn:aws:s3:::<customer-bucket>), s3:GetObject (on arn:aws:s3:::<customer-bucket>/*), kms:Decrypt (optional, on arn:aws:kms:<region>:<account-id>:key/<key-id>)
Redwood only assumes this role to read objects; no s3:PutObject, s3:DeleteObject, or s3:PutObjectAcl permissions are requested or required."

If you want, I can draft the final one-paragraph answer with those two edits and hand it to you to send. Also flagging to product that this language may show up in contracts for customers that insist on explicit permission lists.

-rishi
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: SIG — Q12b (S3 access) needs clarification

Jordan — thanks for the quick review and the follow-up. Per Rishi's suggestions I updated the language to be explicit about presigned URLs and KMS. Below is the final written statement we've added to the SIG answers; please confirm this meets your procurement team's needs and we'll attach the signed PDF to the questionnaire.

Final SIG statement (for insertion into Q12b):
"Redwood Inference does not require write permissions into customer-owned S3 buckets. For data ingestion, customers may either (a) push objects via presigned URLs generated in the customer environment, or (b) grant a customer-managed cross-account IAM role with read-only permissions (s3:GetObject, s3:ListBucket). Redwood does not rely on presigned URLs for automated server-to-server bulk ingestion in production; customers who require guaranteed provenance should use the cross-account role. When customer-owned KMS customer master keys (CMKs) are used to encrypt objects, Redwood requires kms:Decrypt permission for the provided CMK. If objects are encrypted with Redwood-managed keys or are not encrypted, no customer CMK is required. Redwood only assumes the cross-account role to read objects and does not modify or delete customer data in the bucket."

Attachments: final SIG answers (SIG-Bluebridge-Final-20270405.pdf).

If that looks good, can you reply with a short confirmation (e.g., "approved for SIG") so we can mark this question closed in your questionnaire? If you prefer a 15-minute call to confirm, I can propose Tue 8:30–9am PST.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
